'''Erling Størmer''' (born 2 November 1937) is a [[Norwegian people|Norwegian]] [[mathematician]], who has mostly worked with [[operator algebras]].

He was born in [[Oslo]] as a son of [[Leif Størmer]].<ref name=snl>{{cite encyclopedia|year=2007|title=Erling Størmer|encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon]]|editor=Henriksen, Petter|publisher=Kunnskapsforlaget|location=Oslo|url=http://snl.no/Erling_St%C3%B8rmer|language=Norwegian|accessdate=29 October 2009}}</ref> He was a grandson of [[Carl Størmer]] and nephew of [[Per Størmer]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|year=2007|title=Leif Størmer|encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon]]|editor=Henriksen, Petter|publisher=Kunnskapsforlaget|location=Oslo|url=http://snl.no/Leif_St%C3%B8rmer|language=Norwegian|accessdate=29 October 2009}}</ref> He took his doctorate at [[Columbia University]] in 1963 with thesis advisor [[Richard Kadison]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=30502 |title=Erling Stormer |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=2017-12-28}}</ref> and was a professor at the [[University of Oslo]] from 1974 to his retirement in 2007.<ref name=snl/>

He is a member of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27624|title=Gruppe 1: Matematiske fag|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]|language=Norwegian|accessdate=28 October 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927170150/http://www.dnva.no/c26848/artikkel/vis.html?tid=27624|archive-date=27 September 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=2018-08-25 }}, retrieved 2013-08-05.</ref>
